title: ESMAdam: a plug-and-play all-purpose protein ensemble generator

nodes.text: ESMAdam generates protein conformation ensembles by treating the ESMFold embedding space as a trainable variable and using Adam stochastic optimization to update it under an MSE loss against a given ensemble constraint.
nodes.evidence: Using the ESMFold protein language model ESMFold and ADAM stochastic optimization in the continuous protein embedding space, ESMAdam addresses a wide range of ensemble generation tasks.

nodes.text: ESMAdam rests on the assumption that protein conformation ensembles are latently embedded near the native structure within ESMFold's high-dimensional embedding space.
nodes.evidence: This approach is based on the assumption that protein conformation ensembles are latently embedded near the native structures within the high-dimensional embedding space.

nodes.text: Unlike deep-generative-model-based approaches that are task-specific and require retraining, ESMAdam requires no retraining and adapts to diverse ensemble restraint conditions as a plug-and-play framework.
nodes.evidence: Unlike deep-generative-model-based approaches, it requires no retraining and easily adapts to diverse ensemble restraint conditions

nodes.text: Prior general-purpose diffusion-model ensemble generators degrade significantly as the nonlinearity and dimensionality of ensemble constraints increase, limiting their generalization across complex tasks.
nodes.evidence: the performance of such models declines significantly as the nonlinearity and dimensionality of the ensemble constraints increase, limiting their ability to generalize across complex tasks.

nodes.text: Compared to traditional physics-based methods like molecular dynamics and Monte Carlo simulations, ESMAdam significantly reduces computational time.
nodes.evidence: Compared to traditional physics-based methods, ESMAdam significantly reduces computational time.

nodes.text: On a benchmark of ordered, fast-folding, and intrinsically disordered proteins, ESMAdam guided by radius of gyration and secondary structure distributions reproduced equilibrium free energy surfaces matching ground-truth MD simulations across UMAP collective variables.
nodes.evidence: the ability of ESMAdam to accurately capture the conformational diversity and thermodynamic properties of the protein ensembles.

nodes.text: ESMAdam performs CG-to-all-atom backmapping across CG resolutions without retraining, recovering sidechain torsion distributions from Calpha representations and secondary structure ensembles even from ultraCG models where one bead represents five residues.
nodes.evidence: ESMAdam accurately recovers secondary structure conformation ensembles even under ultraCG conditions where most of the backbone information is absent.

nodes.text: No prior universal backmapping approach combines high accuracy with adaptability across different CG resolutions, a gap ESMAdam addresses.
nodes.evidence: No universal backmapping approach currently combines high accuracy with adaptability across different CG resolutions.

nodes.text: ESMAdam can screen alternative binding modes of flexible protein complexes, demonstrated on the Barnase-Barstar enzyme-inhibitor complex with multiple metastable states.
nodes.evidence: exploring multiple binding modes in flexible protein complexes. The test system is the well-characterized enzyme-inhibitor complex Barnase-Barstar

nodes.text: ESMAdam reconstructs 3D protein structures from cryo-EM density images by using the cryo-EM image as the ensemble constraint within the embedding optimization.
nodes.evidence: reconstructing protein 3D structures from cryo-EM images

nodes.text: Single static structures fail to represent the full spectrum of functional protein states, motivating ensemble generation that captures protein dynamism for catalysis, transport, and signal transduction.
nodes.evidence: single static structures fail to represent the full spectrum of functional states.
